text:
Vancouver's name in the rumor columns this week is Jake DeBrusk. NHLRumors.com ran "The Canucks Will Hold On To Jake DeBrusk for Max Return Close to the Trade Deadline," which tells you how outsiders see his place in the plan, even if nothing has happened.

On the ice he has 13 points (7 goals) in 22 games at about 17 minutes a night, and six of those points came on the power play. That is roughly his usual pace: he scored 23 goals in 81 games last season. He shoots plenty and from good spots, but his 8.87 expected goals (the quality of his chances) say he has finished a little below what he earned.

The worry is five-on-five. With him on the ice, Vancouver has taken only 44% of the expected goals, and his team has scored 4.98 more goals than those chances deserve. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, though it notes he faces top competition with weak linemates. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says 55% of his shots come off the rush. We'd watch whether the even-strength chances follow him, wherever he plays.
